blocks.text: Companies organise products into product lines and Strategic Business Units (SBUs) and review their portfolio regularly to improve positioning, maximise and align investments, clarify resource allocation and improve collaboration.
Portfolio techniques to assess market offerings:
children: BCG matrix: market growth × market share → stars, cash cows, question marks, dogs
GE/McKinsey matrix: industry attractiveness × business unit strength, rated low–medium–high

blocks.text: A/B testing and conjoint analysis are the two main methods to develop new products and to review existing offerings.
Conjoint analysis decomposes preferences for product bundles into part-worths for each attribute level. Clearly defined products are 3.3 times as likely to succeed (Cooper, 1993).
Terminology: attributes, levels, profiles, tasks, part-worths, relative importance. The basic model is additive: total perceived value = sum of part-worths (incl. price).
Example pizza: 324 possible pizzas and 16 parameters; one customer's partial benefits show which pizza he prefers and how he trades toppings against price.

children: Stage 1 – design: select attributes and levels, develop bundles
Stage 2 – obtain data: data collection procedure, part-worth computation
Stage 3 – evaluate: segment customers, market simulations, choice rule, adjust shares for marketing programs

blocks.text: Water bottle exercise: 3 × 3 × 2 × 3 = 54 profiles → efficient design; rating-based conjoint; find best profiles, relative importance, preferred material, market shares (max-utility rule, threshold 4) and the effect of price increases / maximum willingness to pay.
A method for assessing customers' preferences that decomposes preferences for product bundles into preferences (value) for each product attribute option (part-worths).
The contribution of an attribute level to the total perceived value of a profile.
The relative leverage of an attribute on total perceived value: the impact of changing from its worst to its best level.
A hypothetical product or offering, i.e. a set of attributes with specific levels.

Conjoint mini cases appeared in every mock exam (Polkaly, Ralph). Practise: best combination per segment, most important feature (ranges), target segment for a given product, and the effect of a price change.
